title: She escaped with 36 cents... and came back bigger than ever
note: True story: Tina Turner's July 1976 escape in Dallas and her 1984 comeback. Real audio: Tina on the Jonathan Ross Show (2017, OPF9WW7pDVw), CBS / Gayle King (aFKrg9xh0aA, '36 cents'), HBO TINA trailer (w9IkVtLvflU), 1985 Grammys (wCdQm2DUNNk). Never the Angela Bassett film. Abuse non-graphic. Script: tina_turner.script.md.

beats.say: In July 1976, Tina Turner ran across a freeway in Dallas, with thirty-six cents in her pocket. Eight years later, she was one of the biggest stars in the world.
beats.speak: In July nineteen seventy-six, Tina Turner ran across a freeway in Dallas, with thirty-six cents in her pocket. Eight years later, she was one of the biggest stars in the world.

beats.say: She grew up in Nutbush, Tennessee, as Anna Mae Bullock. As a teenager, she started singing with Ike Turner's band.
beats.speak: She grew up in Nutbush, Tennessee, as Anna May Bullock. As a teenager, she started singing with Ike Turner's band.

beats.say: Then Ike put out her first record, under a new name.
She later said he chose it so he could own her. They married, and the hits came. River Deep, Mountain High. Proud Mary, which won a Grammy.
But behind the stage, she later said, Ike controlled everything, and hurt her for years.
Then, in July 1976, on the way to a hotel in Dallas, after another fight, she waited until he fell asleep.
beats.speak: Then, in July nineteen seventy-six, on the way to a hotel in Dallas, after another fight, she waited until he fell asleep.

beats.say: She made it to a Ramada Inn across the freeway. The manager gave her a room.
In the divorce, she gave up almost everything.
She paid off the debts from cancelled shows, lived on food stamps, and sang in small clubs. Her solo albums flopped.
Then in 1983, by her account, David Bowie skipped a record-company dinner, to go and see his favourite singer. The executives followed him, and saw the crowd.
beats.speak: Then in nineteen eighty-three, by her account, David Bowie skipped a record-company dinner, to go and see his favourite singer. The executives followed him, and saw the crowd.

beats.say: In 1984, at forty-four, she released Private Dancer. What's Love Got to Do with It went to number one, her first ever. She was then the oldest woman to top the chart.
beats.speak: In nineteen eighty-four, at forty-four, she released Private Dancer. What's Love Got to Do with It went to number one, her first ever. She was then the oldest woman to top the chart.

beats.say: Four years later in Rio, about a hundred and eighty thousand people came to see her. A Guinness World Record.
She found love again, married in Switzerland, and lived until 2023.
beats.speak: She found love again, married in Switzerland, and lived until twenty twenty-three.

beats.say: So, thirty-six cents, and a run across a freeway... that's how Tina Turner became Tina Turner.
